name: Centro (Rua Coberta & Av. Borges de Medeiros)
tagline: The walkable heart of Gramado's chocolate and fondue scene
description: The central strip along Rua Coberta and Avenida Borges de Medeiros is Gramado's main tourist core, packed with chocolaterias, fondue restaurants, boutique hotels, and Bavarian-styled facades. It is the most walkable base, easy for short-term remote work stints, but also the priciest and most crowded, especially during Natal Luz.
pros: Reliable wifi in hotels and cafes
cons: Very crowded during Natal Luz and holidays

name: Lago Negro
tagline: Pine-lined lake district just south of the center
description: The area around Lago Negro, Gramado's postcard black-water lake ringed by pine and araucaria trees, offers a quieter, more scenic residential feel a short walk or drive from the main strip. Several hotels and cafes here cater to visitors wanting nature views without leaving town, making it a pleasant, calmer alternative base.
bestFor: Longer stays, nature lovers, quieter work sessions
pros: Still close enough to walk to the center
cons: Fewer dining options right at hand

name: Planalto / Bavaria residential district
tagline: Quiet hillside residential streets above the tourist core
description: The Planalto and Bavaria neighborhoods spread across the hills above the center, mixing local residential streets, guesthouses, and small pousadas with sweeping valley views. This area suits nomads wanting a real neighborhood feel, lower prices, and a bit of distance from the tourist bustle, though a car or rideshare becomes more useful here.
bestFor: Budget-conscious stays, longer-term rentals, car-based living
pros: More affordable rentals than the center
cons: Requires a car or rideshare for daily errands
Steep streets and less pedestrian infrastructure

name: Canela
tagline: Gramado's laid-back neighbor with canyon access
description: Just 8km from Gramado, Canela is a smaller, less manicured sister town with its own historic church square, Caracol waterfall park nearby, and generally lower prices. Many nomads base here for a more relaxed, less touristy atmosphere while still day-tripping into Gramado for restaurants and shopping.
bestFor: Budget stays, outdoor access, avoiding Natal Luz crowds
pros: Closer to canyons and waterfall parks
Less crowded even in high season
cons: Still needs transport to reach Gramado's center
